brief.whyItMatters: Your client work is building with models, so a change in how agents, tools or evals behave changes what you can ship and how you test it.

keyConcepts.explanation: A program in which a model picks a tool, reads the result and decides the next step, repeating until the task is done or a limit stops it.
A fixed task set used to compare models. Scores mean little once the tasks leak into training data, so check how contamination was handled.

brief.whyItMatters: The platform is the one dependency every web project shares. A feature reaching all browsers removes a library, and a regression explains a bug you did not write.

keyConcepts.explanation: A label from the web standards community that tells you a feature works in all major browsers, and since when.
A browser API that animates between two DOM states or two pages by snapshotting old and new, with no animation library.

brief.whatHappened: "Tells of a Slop UI" reached the Hacker News front page with 369 points and 233 comments.
brief.whyItMatters: You design and build the same interface. Craft techniques and tool changes shorten the path from a Figma decision to shipped, accessible UI.

keyConcepts.explanation: Named values for colour, spacing and type that design tools and code share, so one change updates every screen.
The curve that maps time to progress in an animation. It decides whether movement reads as mechanical, natural or sluggish.

brief.whyItMatters: The energy and water cost of AI is part of the engineering trade-off. Numbers from real deployments let you argue for a smaller model or a cached answer.

keyConcepts.explanation: The electricity one model request consumes. It depends on model size, hardware and batching, and published figures often leave out training.
Grams of CO2 emitted per kilowatt hour. It changes by region and by hour, so where and when a job runs matters.

items.excerpt: Reasoning models often generate very long reasoning traces, making inference computationally expensive. Existing approaches typically improve efficiency either through inference-time early-stopping mechanisms or by explicitly encouraging shorter reasoning during training, for...

brief.whyItMatters: Research results decide what the next model generation can do. Knowing the method tells you whether a claimed gain will hold for your workload.

keyConcepts.explanation: Training after the base model exists, using examples or feedback, to make it follow instructions, reason in steps or refuse unsafe requests.
